MAJOR: `/admin/migrations/*` claims a 150s budget, but the request-timeout middleware (30s, nothing non-exempt bypasses it) cancels `r.Context()` first, so `migrationCtx`'s 150s is unreachable and the documented knob is dead code; migrations will 504 at 30s.

Graceful drain is `max(WriteTimeout,30s)` = 180s by default, contradicting the acceptance criterion "drains in-flight work on graceful shutdown (30s)"; the doc silently redefines the AC instead of flagging an approved AC change.

`isExempt` (health/ready/metrics) also bypasses the role gate and body limit, so a closed/failed runtime-role guard still serves `/metrics` with pool gauges — observability leaking past a fail-closed posture; exempting quota alone would match the AC.

`s.fail` forwards raw `err.Error()` to clients for all 4xx (JSON decode errors echo request fragments, objpolicy errors echo key material); the narrow redaction regex does not make "messages are redacted" true for these paths.
MINOR: `EnvelopeFallback`'s `fallbackWriter` intercepts *every* 404/405 `WriteHeader`, discarding handler-specific messages ("artifact not found" → "not found") and silently swallowing the original body write — a fragile double-envelope path.
`recoverMiddleware` writes a 500 envelope after headers may already be committed (`statusWriter` suppresses the status change), yielding mixed bodies and no reliable 500 signal.
AC says `/metrics` is "counters only"; implementation ships histograms and gauges and the doc was amended to match — align AC or trim output rather than drifting the contract.
`statusWriter`/`fallbackWriter` implement only `Flush`+`Unwrap`; a future streaming/SSE or hijacking route will fail silently behind this chain.
`peekJSONTenant` buffers up to 1 MiB of every JSON POST purely to read one field; a bounded prefix read would avoid the per-request copy.

Tenant from a JSON body is never cross-checked against `X-Tenant-Id`/query (header silently wins), so attribution can be steered — tolerable only because the global bucket is the control; state this explicitly in the doc.
DB-role recheck tolerates 1 silent failure before closing the guard (`failures >= 2`); a single failed recheck leaves a potentially-demoted role serving traffic for another full interval.
NIT: `config/env-flags.json` was fully re-indented, making the registry diff unreviewable and polluting blame; keep formatting churn out of functional changes.
Doc line `"- **Rollback:** ...` has a stray leading quote, rendering broken markdown.
`subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` short-circuits on unequal lengths, leaking admin-token length; compare digests if this matters.
`weakTokens` is bypassed by trivial variants; the ≥24-char rule plus a charset/entropy check would be more robust than an 8-word denylist.

Two divergent boolean parsing styles in one package: strict `boolean()` for limits flags, permissive `flagEnabled()` for dev/anon flags (the latter is correct fail-closed, but document why they differ).
SUMMARY: Solid overall shape: single shared pool, env-driven validated config, token bucket + concurrency caps with injected clock, versioned envelope, and DB-gated role guard all land with reasonable test coverage, and the language rule is respected.

Top risks: the 150s migration timeout is unreachable behind the 30s request deadline (silent misconfiguration), the 30s-vs-180s drain drifts from the AC without approval, and raw 4xx error strings leak past the redaction guarantee.
Secondary: the 404/405 interception wrapper is a maintainability trap, and the role-gate exemption scope is broader than the AC requires.
